learning_outcomes.text: Demonstrate knowledge of different environmental management tools, both preventive and corrective, to achieve greater sustainability in activities and production processes.
Identify legal requirements for pollution prevention and control applicable to different sectors of activity.
Know and be able to apply standardized environmental management systems, identifying and evaluating environmental aspects and proposing measures to achieve eco-efficient processes and products.
Be able to apply environmental impact assessment methods and know methods for evaluating environmental performance and risk in companies.
Know the methodology of life cycle analysis and eco-design.

syllabus_topics: Environmental impact assessments. Concept, environmental factors and methodology.
Environmental management systems: ISO 14001 and EMAS
Integrated management systems: Quality, environment and safety.

assessment_methods.method: Exercises, assignments and presentations developed during the course (classroom practices)

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated using the scores from exams (40%), coursework (45%), and lab practices (15%). Two partial exams for the expository content are eliminatory and compensable if scoring above 4.5/10, with a minimum of 1.5/5 on each part (theory and exercises) of the exams. For coursework, active participation in classroom tasks counts for 10%, and written reports and oral presentations for 35%. Lab practice evaluation includes student work (50%) and the practice report (50%), requiring a minimum of 4/10 on the report and all individual practice reports. Overall, a minimum of 5 points out of 10 is required to pass the subject. For extraordinary exams, students who did not pass lab practices or coursework in the ordinary session will undergo a practical exam for those components.
